correctness.rationale: Restart renewal normalizes the two discounted exit transforms; a common factor of s cancels with the convention of absorption before reset. Tridiagonal cofactors give the odds as a positive constant times s^(2z-a) times the right-to-left block determinant ratio. Killed-block eigenvalues pair by bipartiteness, with squared nonzero eigenvalues strictly below one. For z<a/2 and a≤10 the smaller block has at most one factor; it either cannot offset the negative power term, or pairing it against the largest opposing factor makes the ratio of its contribution to the remaining positive terms strictly increasing. At the midpoint the two lists have at most two entries each; coordinatewise order gives a fixed sign (or an identically zero derivative), and the crossed case is a difference of two positive terms with strictly monotone ratio. Reflection covers the other starts. I reconstructed the example by exact Cramer's-rule determinants, verified its derivative numerator and all four rational signs, and obtained exactly two roots in (0,1) by a Sturm count. The signs give a strict minimum then a strict maximum; a=11 is 12 total states.
residual_risks: No claim about holding, nongeometric clocks, other reset sites, or the sharp maximum for longer paths.
